## On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods

To prove, check or extend a result of this book, start with its catalog: each of the 186 results has its exact statement, its status (proved, conditional or open), its assumptions, its origin, its printed number and page, and the LaTeX file of its source. The numbers and pages are those of version 1.1.0 of the PDF. Cite the book and the number of the result.

- [On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/index.html.md): by Nick Polson and Vadim Sokolov (2026). What probability can and cannot contribute to the Langlands programme: Sato Tate laws, random walks on trees and isogeny graphs, Thorin measures and generalized gamma convolutions as reformulations of the Riemann hypothesis, and Bayesian identification of Sato Tate groups, with code and data. Keywords: Langlands programme, Sato Tate law, Frobenius traces, automorphic L functions, generalized Riemann hypothesis, Thorin measures, generalized gamma convolutions, random walks on trees, supersingular isogeny graphs, random matrix theory, Poisson Dirichlet law, critical percolation, Bayesian inference.
- [How to cite](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23445874): DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23445874 for version 1.1.0 (10.5281/zenodo.23419247 for all versions); the BibTeX entry is on the book page
- [Results by chapter](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html.md): 186 results with their statements, status and numbers

- [All facts as JSON](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/langlands/main/site/book.json): title, authors, DOIs, licenses, links, citation, chapters with summaries, and every result with its printed number, page, source file and LaTeX label

- [Main result: Equidistribution does not determine automorphy](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#equidistribution_does_not_determine_automorphy): Proposition 1.5, page 7, proved. Sato Tate equidistribution of a sequence indexed by the primes cannot certify that it comes from a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL(2) with trivial central character, because altering such a sequence on an infinite set of primes of density zero leaves the limiting empirical averages of all continuous functions unchanged but, by Ramakrishnan's refinement of strong multiplicity one, makes it nonautomorphic, and continuum many equidistributed sequences are not automorphic.
- [Main result: Limit of the normalised Kemeny constants of supersingular isogeny graphs](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#kemeny_constant_supersingular_isogeny_graphs_limit): Theorem 10.6, page 150, proved. As the characteristic grows through primes congruent to 1 modulo 12, with the prime isogeny degree fixed, the mean time for simple random walk on a supersingular isogeny graph to hit a uniformly random curve is asymptotic to the number of vertices times the expected number of visits of simple random walk on the regular tree of the same degree to its starting point, so about twice the number of vertices for 2 isogenies.
- [Main result: Thorin criteria for the generalized Riemann hypothesis of automorphic L functions](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#thorin_criteria_generalized_riemann_hypothesis_automorphic): Theorem 14.8, page 219, proved. The generalized Riemann hypothesis for the L function of a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL(n) over the rationals, and the Riemann hypothesis for zeta, are each equivalent to several positivity statements, among them that the reciprocal of the self dual completion, read in the squared variable, is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution whose Thorin measure sits at the squared ordinates of the zeros, and a Hankel criterion computable from central derivatives; the theorem is an equivalence that extends the first author's 2018 paper, and it proves no case of either hypothesis.
- [Main result: Thorin criterion for the Ramanujan Petersson conjecture at a prime](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#ramanujan_petersson_local_thorin_criterion): Corollary 15.4, page 237, proved. For a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL(2) over the rationals with trivial central character, the Ramanujan Petersson conjecture at an unramified prime (outside the degenerate case of trace 2) holds exactly when the reciprocal of the symmetrised Euler factor, read in the squared variable, is the Laplace transform of a probability law, which is then a generalized gamma convolution whose Thorin measure is a periodic comb (Ramanujan is local Thorin, as the generalized Riemann hypothesis is global Thorin); the corollary is an equivalence and proves no case of the conjecture.
- [Main result: Thorin structure of passage times of the Hecke walk on the regular tree](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#thorin_structure_hecke_walk_passage_times_tree): Theorem 15.15, page 245, proved. The first time that continuous time simple random walk on a regular tree (the Hecke walk, on the Bruhat Tits tree when the degree is a prime plus one) reaches distance n from its start is a generalized gamma convolution whose Thorin atoms, given by the zeros of the sphere polynomials of the tree, lie in the Kesten band and follow the arcsine law as n grows, with an exact mean, a variance linear in n and a central limit theorem; Thorin support in the Kesten band is the random walk form of the Ramanujan bound, and this unconditional theorem about the tree proves no case of the Ramanujan conjecture for automorphic forms.
- [Main result: Gamma process limit of the Frobenius labelled factorisation of a random integer](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#frobenius_labelled_factorisation_gamma_process_limit): Theorem 20.18, page 349, proved. As the parameter of a zeta distributed random integer decreases to one, the logarithms of its prime power factors, multiplied by the parameter minus one and labelled by any equidistributed sequence of points such as Frobenius classes or Sato Tate angles, converge in law to the jumps of a standard Gamma subordinator carrying independent labels drawn from the equidistribution law, and the labelled logarithm converges in law to a Gamma random measure, so that equidistribution becomes a Gamma process.
- [Main result: Extreme value representation of L functions of eta products](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#extreme_value_representation_of_eta_product_l_functions): Theorem 28.7, page 525, proved. For every eta product, that is every product of the functions eta(m tau) raised to nonnegative integer powers r_m with the sum of m r_m equal to 24 (the thirty multiplicative eta products among them), the L function is entire and equals at every complex point the expectation of a regularised incomplete gamma function evaluated at an explicit maximum of exponential clocks, so its values at positive real points are probabilities strictly between zero and one that increase strictly to one.
- [Main result: Consistency of Bayes factors under equidistribution](https://vsokolov.org/books/langlands/results.html#consistency_of_bayes_factors_under_equidistribution): Theorem 30.1, page 555, proved. For any deterministic sequence, such as normalised Frobenius traces, that is equidistributed for a true law with finitely many atoms and finite Kullback Leibler divergence from one candidate law, and with a log likelihood ratio continuous off the atoms, the clipped log Bayes factor between two candidate laws is asymptotically linear in the number of observations, and as the clipping level grows its slope tends to the difference of the divergences of the true law from the two candidates, with no independence assumed.
